newsitem.title: CHINA: China official warns on coin market overheating.
newsitem.headline: China official warns on coin market overheating.

text.p: China coin officials have warned that the coin market is becoming overheated, saying buyers should beware of increasing risk, the Financial News said on Wednesday.

"The current commemorative coin market is not only heating but overheating," the newspaper quoted an official of the China Gold Coin Inc as saying. "More people consider souvenir coin purchasing as a new investment tool now."
The official retail price for a set of gold and silver Three Gorges dam commemorative coins was 6,300 yuan ($759), but now the current market price was 18,000 yuan a set, he said.
The price of a silver commemorative coin for Hong Kong's return to China in July had soared to 4,000 yuan from the official price of 320 yuan, he said.
Speculation on silver panda coins issued in 1996 had pushed the price per coin to 850 yuan from 100 yuan, he said.
The skyrocketing price of coins had spurred people to produce fake coins to earn huge profits, he said.
"Coin buyers should be aware of market risk and be cool-headed to the high price," the official said. He gave no further details.($1= 8.3 yuan)--Beijing Newsroom (8610)6532 1921
